land.text: the western steppe between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya, the Oghuz country of the 700s

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Second Turkic Khaganate; Kangar union'. The Second Turkic Khaganate (682-744) has no dossier.

land.text: the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes, taken from the Kangar union and the Pechenegs 'at the beginning of the 9th century'

predecessors.note: The Kangar union has no dossier; the Oghuz Turks page puts the Oghuz between the Caspian and Aral seas already in the 700s, the Oghuz Yabgu State page only in the early 9th century.

land.text: the Oghuz lands, taken by the Kimeks and Kipchaks (Cumans); Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape of 1056 holds 1,424 of the 1,425 cells

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Seljuq Empire; Kimek Khanate'. The page: Kipchak pressure split the Oghuz; Kimeks and Kipchaks ended the state.

land.text: Khwarezm, from which the Seljuks drove Shah Malik out in 1043

successors.note: The Seljuks split off around 985 and settled at Jend; the Oghuz migration toward Persia in the 11th century was 'led by Tughril and Chaghri Beg' (the Seljuk Dynasty row, 990-1039, and the Great Seljuk Empire row, 1040-1201, carry them).

capitals.name: Yangikent (Jankent)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Yangikent (also spelled Eni-Kent, Yenikent, Djanikand, and others)', 'moved to Yangikent' in the early 9th century (year approximate: 801). The page gives no coordinates and the gazetteer lacks the name: this is a placeholder on the lower Syr Darya ('at the mouth of the Syr Darya'). The page names no earlier capital.

keyframe_review.note: 750-767, 0.45 M km2 (the Caspian-Aral-Syr Darya steppe, 50.2-65.0 E, 40.7-48.0 N). The Oghuz Yabgu State page: 'founded by Oghuz Turks in 750'; the Oghuz Turks page: 'In the 700s, the Oghuz Turks made a new home and domain for themselves in the area between the Caspian and Aral seas' and in northwest Transoxania along the Syr Darya; by 780 'the eastern parts of the Syr Darya were ruled by the Karluk Turks' with the Oghuz to their west. The Oghuz Yabgu State page instead has the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes taken from the Kangar union and the Pechenegs only 'at the beginning of the 9th century'; the pages disagree and the shape is kept. In 766 'after Karluks overran the Türgesh Khaganate in Zhetysu' many Oghuz moved to the Karatau foothills and the Chu valley (outside this shape). Neither page gives an area, so there is no infobox figure to compare.
768-777: the 750 shape without six cells (44.5-45.0 N, 53.2-53.7 E, a Mangyshlak fringe): Cliopatria noise; no page speaks to it. 450,019 km2 unchanged otherwise.
778-782: the six cells return; no page speaks to it.

783-859: the 750 shape again. The Oghuz Yabgu State page: early 9th century, allied with the Karluks and Kimeks the Oghuz 'destroyed the Kangar union and took the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes' and the capital moved to Yangikent; the Oghuz Turks page has the name Oghuz appear in Islamic writers in 813-833. The shape is drawn from 750 and so runs ahead of the Oghuz Yabgu State page by about fifty years.
860-874: the same six-cell fringe change as 768; no page speaks to it.

875-969: the 750 shape. The Oghuz Turks page: 'In the 9th century, the Oghuz from the Aral steppes drove Pechenegs westward from the Emba and Ural River region'; the Pecheneg page has the Oghuz, allied with the Karluks and Kimaks, defeat the Pechenegs near the Aral Sea 'before 850'.

970-989, 0.467 M km2: 61 cells added in the Turgay-Emba steppe (45.4-48.0 N, 53.1-63.2 E). The Oghuz Turks page: 'In the 10th century, the Oghuz inhabited the steppe of the rivers Sari-su, Turgai and Emba'. Five cells at the northern edge drop out. The 970 date is Cliopatria's (ledger event, confidence 1).

990-1045, 0.415 M km2: 171 cells (43.9-46.3 N, 60.8-64.6 E, the lower Syr Darya around Jend) leave the Oghuz and 170 of them lie in Cliopatria's Seljuk Dynasty shape of 990. The Oghuz Yabgu State page: 'Around 985 one of his commanders named Seljuk split off and moved to Jend.' The shape also holds 255 cells of the Khwarezm region (the northern desert fringe) from 750, while the page has Shah Malik conquer Khwarezm only in 1041 (see the new keyframe below); the oasis proper is Ghaznavid and then Seljuk in Cliopatria's other rows.

correction.text: the 990 shape plus Khwarezm, which Shah Malik took from the Ghaznavids

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1041-1042: Shah Malik holds Khwarezm. 'In 1041 Shah Malik conquered Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids' (the ruler list gives 1042); 'The Seljuks drove him out in 1043.' Cliopatria's Seljuk shape already holds the oasis from 1038, so the two rows overlap here and the Oghuz Yabgu State page is followed.

1046-1055, 0.415 M km2: the 990 shape unchanged. The page ends the state in 1055 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1055') although the text says that after the Seljuks drove Shah Malik out in 1043 the state 'likely disappeared'; the Kimek page has the Oguz appear near Kyiv in 1054 pushed by Kipchaks and the Cumans page has the first Rus' contact with Cumans in 1055.

region.text: the Oghuz country between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 750: Oghuz Turks found the Oghuz Yabgu State between the Caspian and the Aral. 'a Turkic state, founded by Oghuz Turks in 750'. The Oghuz Turks page places them in the 700s 'between the Caspian and Aral seas' and along the Syr Darya; the Oghuz Yabgu State page puts the lower Syr Darya in the early 9th century (disagreement noted in the keyframes).

Early 9th century: the capital moves to Yangikent. The Oghuz Yabgu State page gives the century only ('The capital moved to Yangikent'); 801 is the first year of the century. The page names no earlier capital.

region.text: the steppe of the Sari-su, Turgay and Emba rivers, added in the 970 shape

ledger.note: 970: the Oghuz spread over the Turgay-Emba steppe. 'In the 10th century, the Oghuz inhabited the steppe of the rivers Sari-su, Turgai and Emba.' The page gives the century; 970 is Cliopatria's year for the 61 cells.

region.text: the lower Syr Darya around Jend, where Seljuk settled

ledger.note: 985: Seljuk leaves the Oghuz and settles at Jend with his followers. 'Around 985 one of his commanders named Seljuk split off and moved to Jend. His followers became the Seljuks.' Cliopatria's Seljuk Dynasty shape starts in 990 and holds 170 of these 171 cells.
1034: yabghu Shah Malik fights the Seljuks in Khwarezm. 'In 1034-1035 yabghu Shah Malik Barani defeated the Seljuks and Turkomans of Khwarezm.' The page gives the span 1034-1035.

1041: Shah Malik conquers Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids. 'Shah Malik conquered Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids' in 1041 (the ruler list gives 1042). Cliopatria draws the oasis as mostly Ghaznavid before 1038 and Seljuk from 1038.
1043: the Seljuks drive Shah Malik out of Khwarezm. 'The Seljuks drove him out in 1043.' He was later captured and executed and 'the state likely disappeared' (infobox 1055).

1043: the Khwarezm war ends with the Seljuks in possession. Counterpart string follows the contest start; the Cliopatria row 'Seljuk Dynasty' ends in 1039 and the Great Seljuk Empire row continues it.

region.text: the Oghuz lands between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1055: the Kimeks and Kipchaks take the Oghuz lands. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1055'; 'Succeeded by: Seljuq Empire; Kimek Khanate'. Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape holds 1,424 of the 1,425 Oghuz cells from 1056; the Kimek page has the Oguz appear near Kyiv in 1054 pushed by Kipchaks.

region.text: the Oghuz lands between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1055: the Oghuz Yabgu State ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1055'. Kipchak pressure splits the Oghuz; the Seljuk Oghuz enter Persia and found the Great Seljuk Empire (Oghuz Turks page: 'In the 11th century').

wars.name: Oghuz-Karluk struggle for Zhetysu
wars.outcome: After the Karluks overran the Turgesh in Zhetysu in 766 the Oghuz lost the struggle for leadership; many moved to the Karatau foothills and the Chu valley. No border is given.

wars.name: Oghuz war on the Kangar union and the Pechenegs
wars.outcome: Allied with the Karluks and Kimeks, the Oghuz destroy the Kangar union and take the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes, driving the Kangars and Pechenegs west (Oghuz Yabgu State: 'At the beginning of the 9th century'; Pecheneg page: the Oghuz, Karluks and Kimaks defeated the Pechenegs near the Aral Sea 'before 850').
wars.note: The Oghuz Turks page puts the Oghuz in the Caspian-Aral country already in the 700s and the expulsion of the Pechenegs from the Emba and Ural region in the 9th century. Years 800-850 are the pages' bounds, not a campaign date.

wars.name: Oghuz-Rus' war on the Khazars
wars.outcome: 'In 965 the Oghuz State allied with Kievan Rus in a war against the Khazar Kaganate.' No land is named; Khazaria ends in 969 in the khazaria dossier.

wars.name: Oghuz-Rus' war on Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 985 the alliance with Kievan Rus defeated Volga Bulgaria.' No land is named.

wars.name: Oghuz-Seljuk war for Khwarezm
wars.outcome: Shah Malik beats the Seljuks and Turkomans of Khwarezm (1034-1035), takes Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids (1041 or 1042) and is driven out by the Seljuks in 1043.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the page names rivers and seas, not lines. No border is dated more closely than a century except Jend (c. 985) and Khwarezm (1041-1043).

sources.title: Oghuz Yabgu State
sources.note: The state's own article: 750-1055, capital Yangikent, Seljuk at Jend c. 985, Shah Malik and Khwarezm 1034-1043, successors.

sources.title: Oghuz Turks
sources.note: Oghuz Turks: territory in the 700s (Caspian-Aral), 9th-century expulsion of the Pechenegs, 10th-century Turgay-Emba steppe, Seljuks.

sources.title: Pechenegs
sources.note: Pechenegs: the Oghuz, Karluks and Kimaks defeat them near the Aral Sea before 850; Cumans and Torks replace them.

sources.title: Kimek-Kipchak confederation
sources.note: Kimek-Kipchak confederation: Kipchaks push the Oghuz to Kyiv by 1054; successors.

sources.title: Cumans
sources.note: Cumans: first Rus' contact 1055, Pontic steppe.

notes: Not the same state as 'Turks': the Cliopatria rows 'Turks' (666-756, the Western Turks of the Chu and Ili, dossier turks) and 'Oghuz Turks' (750-1055, the Aral and lower Syr Darya) share Wikidata Q2118293 and their shapes touch only at their edges in 750-756. Cliopatria's Wikipedia title 'Oghuz Khagan' is a legendary figure; the state article is the Oghuz Yabgu State, used here. Shapes: nine Cliopatria shapes, but only three changes of substance: 970 (61 cells in the Turgay-Emba steppe, nobody's land, confidence 1 for the year) and 990 (the Jend country, 171 cells, to the Seljuks, which the page dates c. 985), and the end (all 1,425 cells pass to the Kimek-Kipchak row in 1056). The other four are six-cell fringe changes at Mangyshlak (768, 778, 860, 875). No page gives an area (Oghuz Yabgu State: 'Area not given'). Open points: (1) the two pages disagree on when the Oghuz held the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes (700s on the Oghuz Turks page, early 9th century on the Oghuz Yabgu State page); the shape is Cliopatria's from 750; (2) the Khwarezm fringe (255 cells) is drawn as Oghuz from 750, while Khwarezm proper is Ghaznavid then Seljuk in the other rows, and Shah Malik holds it in 1041-1043 only (new keyframe); (3) the page ends the state in 1055 but says it 'likely disappeared' after 1043; (4) the Uzes or Torks, the Oghuz groups that overthrew Pecheneg dominance and crossed the Danube in 1065 (Oghuz Turks page), and the Oghuz near Kyiv in 1054 (Kimek page) are outside the shape; (5) Kimeks and Karluks were allies in the early 9th century and the Karluk dossier (qarlugs, ia-01-f) starts only in 793. (6) matching events other dossiers should carry: seljuk-dynasty (me-09) a gain of the Jend country from this state in 985/990; ghaznavid-empire (me-08) a loss of Khwarezm to this state in 1041 and great-seljuk-empire (me-09) a gain of it from this state in 1043; kimek-kipchak-confederation carries the matching 1056 gain. Counterparts needing dossiers: second-turkic-khaganate (682-744), kangar-union, pechenegs (Pecheneg Khanates 889-1091). Names the gazetteer lacks: Yangikent (capital), Jend (the Seljuk base).
